text: Designing a good REST API is like building a clear road map for developers. First, your endpoints should be simple and logical, using nouns for resources, such as `/users` or `/orders`, instead of verbs. Second, always use standard HTTP status codes to communicate results—`200` for success, `404` if a resource is missing, and `400` for bad requests. This helps clients understand errors without reading the response body. Third, maintain consistent versioning from the start, such as `/v1/users`, so that changes don’t break existing users. Finally, write thorough, up-to-date documentation with examples. Good docs and clean status codes save developers hours of debugging and make your API a pleasure to use.
